item.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.13461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Chien, Nakazato, and Meng that the numerical range of a finite complex matrix has constant width $d$ if and only if it is a closed disk of radius $d/2$, with a singleton allowed when $d=0$. For $d>0$, the characteristic polynomial of the associated Hermitian pencil and its translate by $d$ have a nonconstant common divisor over $\mathbb{C}(\zeta)$. At points on the unit circle where the factorization can be evaluated, every root of the common divisor equals the smallest eigenvalue. A coefficient of the divisor thus gives a rational formula for that eigenvalue. The characteristic equation forces this rational function to be a Laurent polynomial with exponents in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Antipodal symmetry then makes the midpoint of the extreme eigenvalues a first harmonic, giving the support function of a disk. We also obtain the corresponding quadratic factor of the Kippenhahn polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Muyan Jiang

item.title: Banach isomorphism between separable \(L_p\)-spaces, \(1\le p\ne2<\infty\), associated with hyperfinite type III von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.13507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each fixed \(p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}\), the number of Banach isomorphism classes of separable \(L_p\)-spaces associated with hyperfinite type III von Neumann algebras is \(2^{\aleph_0}\).
item.dc:creator: Chenhao Gao, Jinghao Huang, Yunpeng Zhu

item.title: On Isomorphic Embeddings of Noncommutative Lorentz Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that for $0<p_1,p_2,q_1,q_2<\infty$, the Lorentz operator ideal $C_{p_1,q_1}$ embeds isomorphically into $C_{p_2,q_2}$ if and only if (1) $p_1=q_1=2$ or (2) $p_1=p_2$ and $q_1=q_2$, which is in contrast to the classical result that $\ell_{q}$ embeds into $\ell_{p,q}$ as a (complemented) subspace. We also study the isomorphic embeddings between operator ideals generated by the weighted Lorentz sequence spaces $d(w,p)$ ($0<p<\infty$). We characterize those (commutative/noncommutative) Lorentz function spaces $L_{W}^p$ that are isomorphic to subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1\leq p<2$ over some noncommutative probability spaces, which is a noncommutative version of Sch\"utt's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Chenhao Gao, Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev, Zhizheng Yu

item.title: The Fermat--Torricelli problem under isosceles orthogonality-type conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The location problem studied by Weber \cite{Weber} leads to the Fermat--Torricelli problem of minimizing sums of distances. Ben\'{i}tez, Fern\'{a}ndez and Soriano \cite{BFS} proved that a real normed space of dimension at least three is an inner-product space if and only if every triple of points has a Fermat--Torricelli median in its convex hull. Pakhrou \cite{Pakhrou} showed that it suffices to test equilateral triangles. We establish a characterization using triangles $\{0,x,y\}$ satisfying \[ \|x+y\|=\lambda\|x-y\|,\qquad \forall\,\lambda>2/3, \] with the parameter fixed in each characterization. The case of parameter one gives an isosceles orthogonality criterion. The proof combines radial rescaling with the transfer of planar minimality to the ambient space, without completeness or regularity assumptions on the norm.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu

item.title: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. This answers questions due to several open problems in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Yi Gao, Jinghao Huang, Ran Xu

item.title: Frames Associated with $C_0$-Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central question in dynamical frame theory asks when the orbit $\{\Lambda^n f\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ of a vector $f$ under a bounded operator $\Lambda$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ is a frame. Christensen, Hasannasab and Philipp answered it, showing in particular that such an operator must be similar to the compression of the unilateral shift on $H^2(\mathbb{T})$ to a coinvariant subspace. We prove a continuous analogue: if a $C_0$-semigroup $\{T(t)\}_{t\ge0}\subset B(H)$ generates a continuous frame $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$, then the operators $T(t)$ are simultaneously similar to the compressions of the shift semigroup to a fixed coinvariant subspace. Moreover, $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$ is a continuous frame if and only if $\{C^n(I-A)^{-1}\varphi\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ is a frame, where $A$ is the infinitesimal generator and $C=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$ the cogenerator; the frame bounds of the two systems differ by a factor $2$. We also derive necessary conditions for the existence of frame vectors and discuss several examples. Finally, we show that the compressed shift on a model space $K_\theta$ is the cogenerator of a $C_0$-semigroup admitting frame vectors if and only if the inner function $\theta$ has a finite angular derivative at $1$; in that case we describe all frame vectors, and the boundary reproducing kernel at $1$ generates a tight continuous frame.
item.dc:creator: Victor Bailey, Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Jonathan R. Partington

item.title: Frame Measure Rigidity and Fiber Entropy for Homogeneous Self-Similar Measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let N >= 2, 0 < \rho < 1, and let b_0, ..., b_{N-1} be distinct vectors in \mathbb{R}^d. Let \mu be the uniform homogeneous self-similar probability measure generated by the maps S_a(x) = \rho x + b_a, without any separation assumption. We prove that if \mu admits a frame measure, then the conditional coding measure is a Dirac mass for \mu-almost every point. Equivalently, the coding map restricts to a Borel bijection between full-measure subsets of the symbolic space and the attractor. Consequently, the fiber entropy vanishes at every finite level, and \mu is exact dimensional with $\dim_H \mu = \frac{\log N}{-\log \rho} \leq d.$ In particular, \mu admits no frame measure whenever its Hausdorff dimension is strictly smaller than the similarity dimension. This excludes frame measures whenever N\rho^d > 1. As an application, we show that the uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolution on the real line admits a frame measure in the range N^{-1} <= \rho < 1 if and only if \rho = N^{-1}.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Jie Wang

item.title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $\alpha/t$ with $\alpha\geq 1$, and that the trajectory converges to the zero of minimal second moment, which is a Dirac mass, so that the agents reach consensus (all agents reach the same point). Finally, we study a discrete analogue for nonexpansive operators and show that the generated sequence converges to the fixed point closest to a reference Dirac mass; this fixed point is again a Dirac mass, so that consensus is also reached under this scheme. The main arguments rely on a specially tailored superposition principle, which represents the flow as a curve in a fixed Hilbert space of random trajectories, where the crucial estimates are derived.
item.dc:creator: Radu Ioan Bo\c{t}, Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella, Tr\'{\i} Minh L\^e

item.title: On operators with infinitely many spectral components
item.description: arXiv:2611.14394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a unital complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$. We prove that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathscr A$ contains a sequence of non-zero pairwise orthogonal idempotents, and that the number of components of a spectrum is always finite, $\aleph_0$ or $\mathfrak c$. This allows us to extend the spectral depth $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)$ to a cardinal-valued invariant with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\aleph_0,\mathfrak c\}$. We show that $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ precisely when $\mathscr A$ contains a dyadic family of idempotents indexed by the full binary tree. In that case, some element has spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space $\mathbf 2^{\mathbb N}$. The supremum defining $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)$ is attained when the spectral classes of $\mathscr A$ are dense and when $\mathscr A$ is commutative, but not in general. We construct a unital complex Banach algebra with $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ and $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\varnothing$. If $\Delta$ is the character space of a commutative $\mathscr A$ and $\pi_0(\Delta)$ is the space of all components of $\Delta$, then $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\card\bigl(\pi_0(\Delta)\bigr)$ when $\pi_0(\Delta)$ is finite, $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ when $\pi_0(\Delta)$ is infinite and scattered, and $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ when $\pi_0(\Delta)$ is not scattered. We also prove that the spectral depth is additive with respect to finite direct sums and that the spectral classes are invariant under injective holomorphic functions.
item.dc:creator: Janko Bra\v{c}i\v{c}, Marko Kandi\'c

item.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.
item.dc:creator: K\^ohei Sasaya

item.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.
item.dc:creator: Christian K\"ummerle, Dustin G. Mixon

item.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Qin Wang, Chen Zhang

item.title: Universal Approximation Theorem for Metaplectic Neural Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.13991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove universal approximation for metaplectic neural operators on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains. The nonlocal branches are whole-space metaplectic multipliers with zero extension and restriction, associated with any fixed free symplectic matrix. Assuming a smooth, globally Lipschitz, nonpolynomial activation, we obtain compact-uniform approximation of continuous operators from $C^s$ to $C^r$ and from $H^s$ to $H^r$ in the respective output norms, for arbitrary nonnegative integers $s,r$ and finite input and output channel dimensions. In the Sobolev setting, compact input sets must additionally be uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$. One hidden operator layer with one nonlocal branch suffices. A single scalar symbol atom and finitely many positional features are prescribed by the transform and domain independently of the target operator, compact set and accuracy. The proof combines averaging neural operator theory with an exact chirp-conjugated averaging identity and derivative estimates. The result includes Fourier and fixed nondegenerate fractional Fourier multiplier constructions.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Abdeljawad, Malek Yacine Rezoug

item.title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Monod

item.title: Regularity via subequations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).
item.dc:creator: Vasanth Pidaparthy, Yanir A. Rubinstein

item.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.14510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.
item.dc:creator: Van Le, Tuoc Phan

item.title: Isoperimetric Inequality on Manifolds with Quadratically Decaying Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2506.13365v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the reverse-improvement problem for Sobolev inequalities on manifolds with quadratically decaying Ricci curvature. Under volume comparison and relative connectedness of the ends, we show that an $L^2$ Sobolev inequality, together with an $L^p$ Hardy inequality, implies the corresponding $L^p$ Sobolev inequality, including the endpoint $p=1$. We also give a semigroup gluing proof of the two-scale isoperimetric estimate on connected sums with product ends, and an alternative proof of the classical Sobolev inequalities for generalized Grushin gradients.
item.dc:creator: Dangyang He

item.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
item.description: arXiv:2606.17922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.
item.dc:creator: Zhangsong Li

item.title: Plancherel Identities for unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$
item.description: arXiv:2606.27008v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate spectral pairs associated with unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ that are periodic with respect to full-rank lattices. We establish a characterization of such spectral pairs in terms of the spectrality of an associated bounded fundamental component. More precisely, we prove that the Fourier transform defines an isometric isomorphism onto an $L^2$ space with an explicitly determined absolutely continuous pair measure, supported on a union of translates of a dual-lattice fundamental domain, if and only if the bounded component admits an orthogonal basis of exponential functions with frequencies in the dual lattice. In particular, the Plancherel identity alone is sufficient to characterize these spectral pairs. As an application, when the bounded component tiles $\br^d$ by a lattice, we obtain an equivalence between certain translational tiling properties of unbounded periodic sets and the existence of the corresponding Plancherel identities. We also examine periodicity properties of sets that tile by finite translation sets, highlighting distinctions between the one-dimensional and higher-dimensional settings.
item.dc:creator: Dorin Ervin Dutkay, Piyali Chakraborty

item.title: Thin-Shell implies small-ball deviation via Gaussian tilts
item.description: arXiv:2608.20816v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that uniform thin-shell estimates for isotropic log-concave measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ yield precise and explicit deviation estimates for the Euclidean norm $|X|$ below the expectation, improving the square-root dependence of Klartag-Lehec to a quadratic one (which is best possible, up to numeric constants). Using the recent Chen-Klartag sharp variance bound, we deduce: $$ \mu\left(|X|\le \sqrt{n}-s\right) \le \exp\left\{ -\frac{s^2}{4} \left(1+O\left(\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\right) \right\} \qquad \forall\, s\in(0,\sqrt{n}). $$ In particular, this yields a new and transparent proof that Thin-Shell implies Slicing (by passing through small-ball estimates). Our method is based on using central Gaussian tilts, recently introduced by Brazitikos, which may be thought of as a deterministic version of Eldan's stochastic localization. An anisotropic variant (when $\mu$ has general covariance structure) of these deviation estimates is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Silouanos Brazitikos, Emanuel Milman

item.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces: Thompson and Hilbert Geometries of JB-Cones
item.description: arXiv:2609.13620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce standard-norm generalized gyrovector spaces: generalized gyrovector spaces whose norm-value line has the ordinary real operations and whose fixed scalar maps are continuous. We prove that every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of two such spaces extends uniquely to a global bijective gyrometric isometry. The proof combines gyromidpoints, point reflections, continuation of local isometry germs, and monodromy; joint continuity of scalar multiplication is derived, rather than assumed. The class includes all nonzero real normed spaces and standardized M\"obius, Einstein, and proper-velocity models, and is stable under finite and countable $\ell^p$-products. We also obtain bounded mapping-space examples and, under natural continuity assumptions, standard-norm function-space GGVs $C(K,G)$ for compact $K$. These yield non-Hilbertian and hybrid examples. For every unital JB-algebra, the positive invertible cone carries a one-parameter family of standard-norm GGV structures whose gyrometrics are conjugate to Thompson's metric by power maps. The projective positive cone has a parallel family, based on the variation norm modulo the unit, conjugate to Hilbert's projective metric. The projective structures are contractible. Together with global JB-cone isometry classifications, the abstract theorem yields local-to-global extension and classification results for Thompson and Hilbert geometries. Full-rank density matrices and normalized state spaces of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, including the Albert algebra, give concrete projective examples.
item.dc:creator: Jyamira Oppekepenguin

item.title: A New insight into the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak approach to Sobolev maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.04384v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $p \in (1,\infty)$, let $\operatorname{X}=(\operatorname{X},\rho,\mu)$ be a metric measure space such that $(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{d})$ is complete, the measure $\mu$ is uniformly locally doubling and $\operatorname{X}$ supports a weak local $(1,p)$-Poincar\'e inequality. Let $(\operatorname{Y},\operatorname{d},\underline{y})$ be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class (modulo coincidence $\mu$-a.e.) of a Borel map $u:\operatorname{X} \to \operatorname{Y}$ with a separable range belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{Y})$ if and only if $h \circ u$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X})$ for every $1$-Lipschitz function $h:\operatorname{Y} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(\underline{y})=0$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Tyulenev

item.title: Optimum solution to a boundary-value problem for an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$ via measure of noncompactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.13878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncom-pactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.
item.dc:creator: Parveen Kumar, Ankit Kumar

item.title: Non-expansive maps between unit balls that send the sphere onto the sphere are linear isometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be real Banach spaces with closed unit balls $B_X$, $B_Y$ and unit spheres $S_X$, $S_Y$. We prove that every non-expansive map $F\colon B_X\to B_Y$ with $F(S_X)\subseteq S_Y\subseteq F(B_X)$ is the restriction of a surjective linear isometry $X\to Y$. Consequently, a non-expansive bijection of $B_X$ onto itself that fails to be an isometry must map some point of $S_X$ into the open unit ball, so the plasticity of $B_X$ reduces to showing that non-expansive bijections preserve norm 1. The proof shows that $F$ is Fr\'echet differentiable at $0$ with a surjective linear isometry $T$ as its derivative, and then proves $T^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$ using a quantitative rigidity lemma for non-expansive self-maps $H$ of $B_X$ satisfying $\|a+H(a)\|=2$ for $a\in S_X$; the latter relies on the Baillon-Bruck rate of asymptotic regularity for Krasnosel'skii-Mann iterations. As a corollary, the identity is extremal in the set of non-expansive self-maps of $B_X$ for every Banach space $X$, which together with a result of Bargetz, Dymond and Pirk shows that all surjective isometries of $B_X$ are extremal, answering a question of theirs, including the case of $L^1[0,1]$.
item.dc:creator: Kaarel August Kurik

item.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators and prove a zero-product result.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Adhikari, Susmita Das, Shubham Jain, Jaydeb Sarkar

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas

item.title: A Weak Topology on Metric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.19368v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use metric functionals to construct a topology on metric spaces that induces $d$-weak convergence. We show that this topology is invariant under surjective isometries and characterize its convergence in terms of weak metrics. We prove that the topology is $T_1$ on every metric space. For normed linear spaces, we further show that it is Hausdorff and coarser than the classical weak topology. Finally, we construct a sequence in $C[0,1]$ that is unbounded in the sup-norm yet converges $d$-weakly, thereby correcting an assertion in an earlier work.
item.dc:creator: Armando W. Guti\'errez, Olavi Nevanlinna

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis
